ev.q: In May 2004, CDC mailed surveys to 5,386 clinicians in seven specialties who commonly provide STD diagnosis, treatment, and prevention services.
81% reported usually or always asking about the sexual behavior of their adolescent patients to assess STD risk.
90% of clinicians reported usually or always recommending that their adolescent patients use condoms
Nearly all (95%) respondents believed that practicing monogamy or limiting the number of sex partners was highly effective
most of the clinicians assessed STD risk in their adolescent patients
adolescent medicine and family practice physicians were significantly more likely to agree that abstinence was worthwhile to recommend
clinicians were more likely to rate abstinence, monogamy, and limiting number of sex partners as highly effective compared with condom use
CDC mailed surveys to 5,386 clinicians in seven specialties
Stratified sampling by specialty was conducted to enable comparisons among specialties.

methods_quotes.q: Analyses were weighted to adjust for disproportionate sampling by specialty and nonresponse.
